bridges.description: Christianity is more reasonable if its account of God, reason, morality, suffering and history explains the evidence better than the atheistic alternatives considered.
The specifically Christian conclusion depends on historical warrant for Jesus, especially the resurrection, rather than generic theism alone.
Christianity gains comparative support if it supplies coherent grounds for rational inquiry, moral value, meaning and hope.
Atheism is more reasonable if evidence against a perfectly good God and against distinctive Christian claims outweighs Christianity's proposed explanations.
The amount and severity of apparently preventable suffering count as probabilistic evidence against an omnipotent, omniscient and perfectly good deity.
Christianity is less reasonable if its historical, scriptural or moral claims conflict with evidence or defensible moral principles.

sections.title: Comparative standards and worldview scope
sections.rationale: The motion requires standards for reasonable belief, a precise definition of atheism, distinct burdens for atheism and Christianity, and awareness that the two do not exhaust all worldviews.

sections.title: Evil, freedom and final justice
sections.rationale: Tooley's central evidential case concerns preventable suffering; the replies address moral grounding, limits on harmful freedom, finality of judgment and promised justice.

sections.title: Science and rational inquiry
sections.rationale: The exchange distinguishes scientific compatibility, mechanism and agency, rational reliability, empirical testing of Christianity and evidence for common descent.

sections.title: Ultimate explanation and complexity
sections.rationale: Audience discussion isolates whether ultimate reality may be eternal, whether explanatory simplicity favors naturalistic histories, and whether information supports agency.

sections.title: Biblical history and reliability
sections.rationale: The speakers dispute historical interventions, composite-source arguments, scriptural genre and the reliability of miracle testimony.

sections.title: Prophecy and supernatural evidence
sections.rationale: A sustained exchange tests alleged return predictions and competing interpretations, while audience answers qualify the evidential status of possession reports.

sections.title: Morality, atonement and meaning
sections.rationale: The debate addresses objective value, Christian moral doctrines, substitutionary atonement, divine participation in suffering, forgiveness and ultimate meaning.
